title: Factors Affecting of the Good Agricultural Practices for Dairy Cattle Farm of Members’s Kuiburi Dairy Cooperatives Limited, Prachuap Khiri Khan Province / ปัจจัยที่มีผลต่อการปฏิบัติทางการเกษตรที่ดีสำหรับฟาร์มโคนมของสมาชิกสหกรณ์โคนมกุยบุรี จำกัด จังหวัดประจวบคีรีขันธ์
author: Chanapron Prasertwattana; ชนาพร ประเสริฐวัฒนะ; Songserm Homglin; ส่งเสริม หอมกลิ่น; Sukhothai Thammathirat Open University; songserm.hom@stou.ac.th
category: การส่งเสริมและการผลิต
abstract: The objectives of this research are to 1) study the general conditions of members of Kui Buri Dairy Cooperative Limited. 2) Study the dairy farm management of cooperative members. 3) Compare the costs and returns of farm management. Dairy cows during and not during good agricultural practices for dairy farms 4) Analyze factors affecting the practice and non-practice of good agricultural practices for dairy farms, and 5) Study the problems, obstacles, and recommendations for good agricultural practices for dairy farms of members of the Kui Buri Dairy Cooperative Limited.This research is exploratory research. The population used in the study is 60 members of Kui Buri Dairy Cooperative Limited, studied from the entire population. The research instrument used is a questionnaire. The statistics used to analyze the data include frequency, percentage, minimum-maximum values, mean, standard deviation, multiple regression analysis, and content analysis.The research findings show that 1) The majority of cooperative members are male (51.70%) and female (48.30%), with an average age of 47.97 years. Most members have completed primary education (41.70%), with an average cooperative membership duration of 11.22 years. The average household income is 3,725 baht, and the average household expenditure is 16,575 baht. The average duration of dairy farming as an occupation is 15.60 years. The majority of the costs are for dairy cow feed, averaging 90,299.50 baht. The average monthly milk production is 8,590.60 kilograms. The average income from selling milk is 186,551.24 baht. The overall attitude toward agricultural practices in dairy farming is at a very important level, with an average of 3.60. 2) Farm management according to Good Agricultural Practices (GAP) for dairy farms. Most members were unable to comply with record-keeping for dairy cows. 29 members complied with GAP, while 31 did not. 3) Comparison of total costs and returns between those who complied with GAP and
